definitions.gloss: every one of them; without exception; utterly
definitions.explanation: Says that something applied to all members of a set, leaving none out. It is a formal, somewhat literary adverb and most often appears with negative or unfortunate outcomes — plans that all failed, opinions that all clashed.

examples.japanese: {計画|けいかく}はことごとく{失敗|しっぱい}した。
examples.english: Every one of the plans failed.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{意見|いけん}は{私|わたし}のものとことごとく{対立|たいりつ}する。
examples.english: His opinions clash with mine on every single point.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}で{畑|はたけ}の{作物|さくもつ}はことごとくだめになってしまった。
examples.english: The typhoon ruined every last crop in the field.

notes:
Formal and slightly literary; common in writing, news, and speeches, but rare in casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ことごとく{失敗|しっぱい}する: to fail every time
- ことごとく{反対|はんたい}する: to oppose at every turn
- ことごとく{裏切|うらぎ}られる: to be betrayed in every expectation
- ことごとく{打|う}ち{砕|くだ}かれる: to be utterly shattered

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {全|すべ}て: all — the neutral everyday word, with no literary flavor
- {残|のこ}らず: without leaving any behind — plainer, and used for pleasant outcomes too
- {一|ひと}つ{残|のこ}らず: every last one — emphatic and conversational
